_comment: THE HST-core Embedded ABI, machine-readable. Single source of truth.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Thirteen functions times N languages, hand-written, is
13N places for a signature to drift, and drift in an FFI declaration does not
raise a type error -- it corrupts memory or silently reads the wrong field. The
estate has already paid for the general version of this lesson: a retracted rule
survived a docs pass because one field name did two jobs, and an int32/size_t
offset-width mismatch in the harness understated the product for months.
So: bindings are GENERATED from this file, and validate.py fails when the built
library's exports and this manifest disagree. A binding nobody generated from
the manifest is a binding nobody can prove matches the library.
PROVENANCE OF THE VERSION. embedded/exported.linux.map declares HSTCORE_1.4,
and commit 4b1c4bb bumped 1.3 -> 1.4 to add hst_apply_shadow. A libhstcore.so
found exporting 1.3 is a STALE BUILD, not a different ABI -- that exact skew was
live on 2026-08-05 (a .so at 1.3 beside a Python binding declaring 1.4).
Note also: 4b1c4bb's message says '12 total'. There are THIRTEEN. Counted from
the version map, which is the artifact the linker reads.

_typeVocabulary.handle: hst_ctx* — opaque, owned by the library, freed by hst_close
_typeVocabulary.cstring_in: const char* — UTF-8, borrowed for the call
_typeVocabulary.cstring_return: const char* — static storage, never freed by the caller
_typeVocabulary.char_buf_out: char* — caller-allocated, paired with the next size param
_typeVocabulary.status: int — 0 success, negative error; see errors[]
_typeVocabulary.f64_array_out: double* — caller-allocated, may be NULL where noted
_typeVocabulary.f64_array_return: const double* — zero-copy view into library memory, invalidated by the next mutating call

functions.name: hst_open
functions.doc: Open a session from a compiled operator artifact. Takes a licence token, but as of 2026-08-06 that token is only checked by a separate, metered build of the same library -- the community build (Apache-2.0, unmetered, in an HST Studio download's bin/) compiles the check out and opens on an empty token. Where checked, returns NULL on invalid/expired licence, an operator larger than the licence permits, or an unreadable artifact, and writes a short reason into errbuf.

functions.name: hst_open_batched
functions.doc: As hst_open, but the session carries `batch` independent right-hand-side lanes (1..32) under the same operator and the same delta sparsity pattern. All state and delta buffers are LANE-INTERLEAVED: state[row*batch + b], vals[i*batch + b]. Batching amortizes the sparse index traversal across lanes, which is where HST beats a plain exact delta.

functions.name: hst_apply_delta
functions.doc: Apply a sparse delta of n entries to the held state, in-process, no serialization. Column cols[i] changes by vals[i*batch + b] in lane b.

functions.name: hst_apply_shadow

errors.meaning: licence carries no shadow-apply grant (max_shadow_applies <= 0), checked unconditionally on every call

functions.warning: SHARES held state with hst_apply_delta on the same handle. Never interleave shadow and production applies on one hst_ctx — open a SEPARATE handle for shadow validation. Shadow rights come exclusively from the signed licence token; no argument, env var or flag can enable shadow mode.
functions.doc: Shadow-mode apply: identical numerics to hst_apply_delta, metered against max_shadow_applies instead of max_applies, and does not touch applies_used. This is the primitive SHADOW mode is built on.

functions.name: hst_batch
functions.doc: Number of right-hand-side lanes for this handle (1 for hst_open).

functions.name: hst_output_dim
functions.doc: Output dimension N of the operator (rows). The held state buffer has N*batch doubles, lane-interleaved.

functions.name: hst_input_dim
functions.doc: Input dimension M of the operator (columns).

functions.name: hst_state
functions.warning: Zero-copy view into library memory. Valid only until the next hst_apply_delta / hst_apply_shadow / hst_set_state / hst_close. A binding that hands this to a garbage-collected language MUST copy it.
functions.doc: Zero-copy read of the current dense output state, lane-interleaved.

functions.name: hst_set_state
functions.warning: Sets ONLY the output state y. The internal INPUT state x — what hst_recompute_full computes A*x from — is separate. Priming y alone leaves x at pristine zero, and hst_recompute_full would disagree with y by exactly A*x0 forever. ALWAYS pair with hst_set_input using the same baseline. hst_recompute_full returns -5 rather than a silently wrong vector when the two were not primed together.
functions.doc: Set the internal dense output state.

functions.name: hst_set_input
functions.warning: Pair with hst_set_state using the corresponding baseline output. Priming only one of the pair leaves the handle in a state hst_recompute_full refuses to use.
functions.doc: Set the internal dense input state x — the buffer hst_recompute_full computes A*x from. There is otherwise no way to set it other than accumulating one apply at a time from a pristine zero start.

functions.name: hst_recompute_full

errors.meaning: refused: held input state x and output state y are not known to be consistent — set_state was called without a matching set_input, or vice versa

functions.doc: Reference baseline: recompute the full dense output A*x from scratch for the current held input state — the 'before' in a before/after comparison. NOT metered: this is the correctness reference the delta path is checked against, not the product hot path. This is what makes an in-process exactness assert possible, and therefore what SHADOW mode reports against.

functions.name: hst_close
functions.doc: Release a handle. Safe on NULL.

functions.name: hst_version
functions.doc: Library version string, e.g. 'hstcore 1.4.0'. Static storage; never freed by the caller.

_semanticInvariants: LANE INTERLEAVING is the single most commonly mis-bound detail: state[row*batch + b] and vals[i*batch + b], not lane-major. A binding that gets this wrong produces plausible numbers that are wrong, which is the failure class this estate has been bitten by repeatedly.
hst_state() returns a BORROWED pointer invalidated by the next mutating call. Every managed-language binding must copy.
hst_set_state and hst_set_input must be called TOGETHER or not at all.
Shadow and production applies must never share a handle.
